```js
/**
 * Closes the tab with the given key. The remaining tabs keep their keys, so closing leaves a gap (`t1,t3`).
 * @param {{ next: number, tabs: Array<{ key: string, title: string }> }} state Tab strip state; not mutated.
 * @param {string} key Key of the tab to close, e.g. `"t2"`. A key that matches no tab closes nothing.
 * @returns {{ next: number, tabs: Array<{ key: string, title: string }> }} A new state with the same `next` and the
 * tab removed. When no tab has `key`, still a new object, with a new `tabs` array holding the same tabs.
 */
```

- **Recorded decisions:** only `src/tabs/PRECEDENT.md` applies. It says tab keys are never reused or renumbered, so closing a tab leaves a gap. The comment states this and doesn't conflict with it. No PRECEDENT file sets a rule for comment or JSDoc style.
- **Style is the subagent's choice:** the repo has no JSDoc anywhere, only one-line `//` comments, so it used the standard `@param` / `@returns` form. `closeTab` is now the only documented function in the file. If you want a shared `@typedef` for the state shape or a different tag style, say so.
- **Unknown key:** if no tab has that key, `closeTab` still returns a new state object. Code that checks for changes by object identity (React state updates, for example) will treat it as a change. The comment says so and the code is unchanged. The tests don't cover this case.

**1. Diff**
```diff
diff --git a/src/tabs/tab-keys.mjs b/src/tabs/tab-keys.mjs
index 830a094..eb478ce 100644

@@ -9,6 +9,13 @@ export function openTab(state, title) {
   return { next: state.next + 1, tabs: [...state.tabs, { key, title }] };
 }
 
+/**
+ * Closes the tab with the given key. The remaining tabs keep their keys, so closing leaves a gap (`t1,t3`).
+ * @param {{ next: number, tabs: Array<{ key: string, title: string }> }} state Tab strip state; not mutated.
+ * @param {string} key Key of the tab to close, e.g. `"t2"`. A key that matches no tab closes nothing.
+ * @returns {{ next: number, tabs: Array<{ key: string, title: string }> }} A new state with the same `next` and the
+ * tab removed. When no tab has `key`, still a new object, with a new `tabs` array holding the same tabs.
+ */
 export function closeTab(state, key) {
   return { ...state, tabs: state.tabs.filter((tab) => tab.key !== key) };
 }
```
